## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `edbee340d45883b5d04794ac43e6a9694655fa1e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0066-unified-authorization-model.md + none
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: none

PR #37621, card #37245: the one row claimed in 7196224618 (row comment 7178404228, its anchor half). First record on this head, a full round. Read for it: the card body and all 10 of its comments, the PR body, file list and net diff against `main` (`54d6726c09`, merge-base `58570d8002`), the 49 check-runs on the head, and the tree of draft PR #37371 at `71a5990508` (read, not reviewed). The dispatch order was not read.

Check-runs on the head, read 2026-11-26T16:02Z: 49 in all, 26 success, 23 skipped, none red, none pending. A first read at 15:58Z still had `Test Core (1/10)` running; it and `Test Core` have since concluded success.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The diff is one sentence.** One file, +1/−1, and inside line 146 only the words between "The vote is cast inside" and ", so both field merges answer the same" differ (file blob `a3a6e1da85` to `6398170231`). Right: nothing else in the 2026-11-24 note and no other note moves.
- **Accept-set and public surface: none implied.** No schema, export, gate or rule on what a seat may do is in the diff. `Clause-②: no` is right.
- **Decision text: untouched.** D2 ⑧ and the rulings the note records read as before. The sentence changes how the vote function is pointed at, not what the note decides. Right.
- **Anchor population: one out, one in.** `effective-object-permissions.ts#superuserFieldVote` leaves and `effective-object-permissions.ts#holdsViewAllFields` arrives, same file. Right: at the head no symbol anchor under `docs/adr/**` names `superuserFieldVote` any more; lines 142 and 144 keep the name in prose, which is no anchor.

### ② Semver level

- Nothing is published by this diff: no package ships `docs/adr/**`. No `package.json` in the tree names that path, and `os-dev.md` lists it among the paths that publish nothing. No changeset is owed, and `skip-changeset` says what is true. `Check Changeset` concluded success on the head.
- `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` in the PR body are both true of the diff: it changes nothing a metadata author can write and nothing a consumer can call.

### ③ Boundary flags

Open questions of report 7196910014:

- **Q1, a name-free sentence or one that also records the old name: A, keep it as pushed.** Reasons and the one carry are in ④.
- **Q2 (1), the first line `Refs #37245 (one item: …)`: leave.** It is the spelling `execution-duties.md` gives a partial landing (`Refs #N (item k)`, never `Fixes`), the card must stay open for its other rows, and `PR-body guards (claim · duplicate · Part-of · single-writer path)` concluded success on it.
- **Q2 (2), all 21 derived gate commands run locally: leave.** `os-dev.md` names the `--commands` list as the gate families a dev runs for the files it changed; running more than the dispatch asked changes nothing in the PR.
- **Q2 (3), `skip-changeset` hung in the `pr_create` stroke: true on the merits, escalated to the seat on the authority.** The label's premise holds (② above). Whether the dispatch's label sentence or its changeset sentence governed is the seat's to say at L1: the dispatch order is outside this review's inputs, and `os-dev.md` reads "write nothing and report" where a dispatch forbids labels.
- **Q3, the claim's `Metadata-protocol: n/a — docs only`: A, the seat amends the claim line to `none`, a card-side stroke.** The value is outside the closed vocabulary of the claim template in `SKILL.md` (added, narrowed, semantic, none). Every caller of that line's one reader found under `scripts/` on `main` hands it a PR body or a changeset body (`readMetadataProtocolLine` in `clause2-line.mjs`, called by `l1-face.mjs`, the queue guard, the merges audit, the release-notes script and the two changeset gates); none was found that parses a claim comment. So the PR body is right as it stands and the head does not move.

Dev flags (`deviations`, `out_of_scope_findings`):

- Local branch name, commit trailers, PR footer form, the PR template's checklist left out, the reads beyond the card, the environment note: none touches the contract or the reviewed file. They are the seat's L1 reads. The PR head ref is the claimed branch `claude/project-thread-kgrra6`.
- Protocol line written `none` and not copied verbatim: right, see Q3. A verbatim copy would have put an ungradeable value in the PR body.
- Lines 142 and 144 name `superuserFieldVote` in prose, and lines 142 to 146 say View All and Modify All vote on fields and that the end state is not built: confirmed true on `main` and dated the day #37371 merges. Not this PR's to fix. It stays with the unchecked half of the row on #37245 (the D2 ⑧ end-state note, written after #37371 merges).
- The #37371 branch needs one merge of `main` after this lands: confirmed from its tree. Its ADR-0066 blob is `main`'s old one (`a3a6e1da85`), so its anchor gate stays red until that merge. Carrier: seat 7.
- The primary checkout's stale local branch: housekeeping, the seat's.

SQL push-down: the diff holds no code, so nothing to check.

Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]` through the relay; no other login to name.

The security line above reads yes on purpose. The changed sentence states where a permission field vote is cast and that both field merges agree on it, which is permission behaviour by the template's rule. It teaches nothing new: the code it describes is unchanged, and no reading of the note gets wider or narrower. The PR is Tier H whichever way that line reads, because an in-place edit is not an add-only note. No exploitable issue was found; no private findings file was written.

### ④ Design judgment

`docs/adr/0066-unified-authorization-model.md`, line 146, the sentence at the head:

"The vote is cast inside the one function that calls `holdsViewAllFields` (`packages/core/src/security/effective-object-permissions.ts#holdsViewAllFields`), and both field merges call that function, so both field merges answer the same."

Each clause against the code, on both trees. The anchored file is blob `a105b3c534` at the merge-base, at `main` `54d6726c09` and at the head, and blob `b4c72981bb` at #37371's head `71a5990508`.

| Clause | `main` and this head | #37371 at `71a5990508` |
|:---|:---|:---|
| "the one function that calls `holdsViewAllFields`" | one call site, line 1076, inside `superuserFieldVote` (line 1065); the predicate is not exported, so no other file can call it | one call site, line 1064, inside `viewAllFieldsReadVote` (line 1056); not exported |
| "The vote is cast inside" it | a set that holds the bit, with no `readable: false` row of its own on the field, turns the function's read answer to yes and adds no edit | the same two tests; the function answers true |
| "both field merges call that function" | `buildEffectiveFieldPermissions`, line 1175; `PermissionEvaluator.getFieldPermissions`, `permission-evaluator.ts` line 590; each once per field | line 1160; line 566; each once per field |
| "so both field merges answer the same" | both apply that one answer | both apply that one answer |
| the anchor `#holdsViewAllFields` | `function holdsViewAllFields(` at line 1099: a declaration by the resolver's first pattern, in code, not in a comment | the same declaration at line 1086, body identical |

Every clause is true on both trees.

- **It claims no end state.** The sentence says nothing of View All or Modify All. On `main` the function it describes also casts their votes; on #37371 it casts the `viewAllFields` vote alone. The sentence is true of both because it asserts neither, and "both field merges call that function" does not say only they do (on `main`, `conditionedFieldEntries` calls it too).
- **It stays true across #37371's merge.** #37371 changes no file under `docs/adr/**` and neither anchor-gate script, so a merge of `main` carries this sentence in unchanged. On #37371's tree the one `#superuserFieldVote` anchor left anywhere is this line; the liveness ledger there already cites `#holdsViewAllFields` beside `#viewAllFieldsReadVote`.
- **First consumer.** The step `ADR symbol anchors resolve (no line numbers survive)` in `Lint · docs & code guards` concluded success on the head, and that lane's closing step reads each gate's own outcome. `ADR anchors + number uniqueness`, `ADR index is current` and `Check ADR cross-links` concluded success too.
- **Execution plan.** The row orders this PR onto `main` before #37371 leaves draft. Nothing in either tree stands in the way of that order.
- **An edit inside a dated note, not an appended note.** The card's general shape is append-only notes. The row (7178404228, "re-point the anchor") and the claim (7196224618) order exactly this in-place re-point, and a dead anchor can be mended nowhere else. No decision text is touched, and the PR body says plainly that it is an edit. Held; the maintainer reads it before his own merge.

**Open question 1, ruled: A. The name-free sentence loses nothing the note needs.**

- The note needs two things from this sentence: a checkable pointer to where the vote is cast, and why the two merges cannot disagree. Both are there, and both are now true on either tree.
- The name is one step from the anchor on either tree. The doc comment on the anchored declaration names its one reader: `superuserFieldVote` on `main`, `viewAllFieldsReadVote` on #37371. On `main` the notes two and four lines above (142, 144) also carry the name with its file.
- Option B would add a name no gate checks, that stops matching the code the day #37371 merges, at the price of one more push on a governed path.
- Carry, for the row's other half and not for this head: the end-state note should say in words that `viewAllFieldsReadVote` replaced `superuserFieldVote`, because from that merge on lines 142 and 144 name a function the tree no longer has.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

- N1 (nit, accepted as is). "The one function that calls `holdsViewAllFields`" is true of the declaration the anchor names. `packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.ts` declares a second function of the same name, with its own caller (`objectWideFieldVote`); only the path in the parentheses tells the two apart. The count of callers is prose that the anchor gate does not check; the declaration's own doc comment backs it on both trees. No effect on correctness.
- N2 (nit, prose, accepted as is). "Both field merges" stands twice in the one sentence. Not worth a push on a governed path.
